label: First copy step (input = orig token 0, right after <DEL>) in very short sequences (L=3, weaker L=4)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely (98% of mass) at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, prev_tok <DEL>, input is the fed-back first original token, output is orig(1)). Strongly gated by length: L=3 holds 78% of mass (about 40% of L=3 such steps are active... precision 0.73), L=4 holds 22% at a much lower rate, L>=5 essentially never. Small residual at recall_idx 2 for L=3/4 (to_go 0/1). Never fires in the original or delimiter phase. Magnitude is modulated by the identity of the first token: d, w, k, r, b give the strongest activations (top examples all d/w first, e.g. d c j <DEL> [d]); more digits in the sequence lowers it. Predicate (recall_idx==1 & L==3) gives dev F1 0.64, mass recall 0.76; widening to L<=4 gets recall 0.94 but precision 0.18, because L=4 activation depends on first token.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: d, w, k, r, b, m; least: x, v, 1, j) and the third original token (most: j, c, e, 1, h, f; least: k, p, m, w); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=4, L=3, recall_idx=1.
